subject: MerchantLane hosted pricing: post-demo numbers & next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@merchantlane.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: MerchantLane hosted pricing — follow-up & quick numbers request

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and two asks so we can get you a concrete hosted API proposal: 

1) Can you confirm expected monthly token volume (best guess / range) over the next 12 months? If you have a high/low please include both.
2) What are your expected peak TPS characteristics? We care about 99th percentile sustained windows (e.g., 5–15m peaks) and typical average QPS.

From the call I captured: product-facing chat + summarization for support tickets, bursty windows around release days. If you can attach a short CSV (timestamps + token counts) that would be ideal.

For context — our commercial teams usually propose banded unit pricing with optional burst capacity for customers with 1) large monthly volume and 2) high 99th TPS spikes. If I have the numbers above I can put together:
- 1-page dollars-per-1M token recommendation (3 bands)
- suggested burst policy (burst credits or temporary capacity)
- a sample canary/30-day pilot commitment to validate latency and unit economics

Thanks — I’ll assemble a draft and loop Marissa for pricing/ops input.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: request_template.csv (please fill if useful)
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@merchantlane.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MerchantLane hosted pricing — follow-up & quick numbers request

Diego — great to speak. Answers below and attached a simple usage snapshot we pulled from our STAGING telemetry (timestamps are UTC).

- Expected monthly token volume (next 12mo): 110,000,000 — 150,000,000 tokens per month (range reflects ramp and two pilot customers we expect to onboard by Q3).
- Peak TPS (observed / expected): baseline average 65 TPS; 95th ~210 TPS on weekday afternoons; 99th short windows (2–10m) hit ~420 TPS during internal load tests and during product releases.
- Budget guidance: internal stakeholders are targeting ~$800–$1,200 per 1M tokens (we included a ballpark to check fit).

We attached merchantlane_usage_snapshot.csv. Procurement is looped (procurement@merchantlane.com) to start contracting questions. Primary goals for us: predictable per-token cost, clear behavior during bursts, and an SLA for 99th latency for inference.

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the file.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Integrations — MerchantLane
Attachments: merchantlane_usage_snapshot.csv
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: MerchantLane hosted pricing — follow-up & quick numbers request

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Alex’s reply + usage snapshot. Key asks: MerchantLane expects ~110–150M tokens/mo with 99th spikes up to ~420 TPS. They indicated a target budget band ~$800–$1,200 per 1M.

Questions for pricing:
- Given the volume + spikes, what banded $/1M would you recommend? Please include both hosted API standard pricing and a recommended reserved/dedicated option (they care about predictable throughput and 99th latency).
- Should we propose a 30-day pilot with a small committed token amount and burst credits? If so, recommend a pilot structure (commit, unit price, burst cap).

Attaching our current pricing options v3 (redwood_pricing_options_v3.pdf). I’ll keep Alex on this thread so they see the timeline.

Thanks — Diego
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_pricing_options_v3.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@merchantlane.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MerchantLane hosted pricing — forward and recommendation

Thanks Diego — reviewed the snapshot. Proposed recommendation below (concise so we can get a formal quote out today):

Pricing recommendation (hosted API):
- Band A (<= 75M tokens/mo): $1,250 per 1M tokens
- Band B (75M–125M tokens/mo): $980 per 1M tokens
- Band C (>125M tokens/mo): $840 per 1M tokens

Notes:
- MerchantLane’s expected band (110–150M) maps to Band B/C mix. Given their $800–$1,200 target, we can offer an introductory 3-month blended price of $950 per 1M for a 100M committed pilot to demonstrate economics and latency.
- Peak TPS: their 99th windows (~420 TPS) are high relative to baseline; recommend including burst credits (automatic prefix caching + 1 minute of burst capacity at no extra per-token charge for the pilot) and the option to transition to Dedicated if 99th latency overruns are observed.
- SLA/ops: include 99th latency SLO for pilot (with escalation path) and 4-hour support during high-impact release windows.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Diego: send a short commercial summary (1 pager) with the 100M pilot at $950/1M and the three-band table attached.
2) Alex: confirm procurement windows and whether MerchantLane requires PO-based billing or DocuSign SOW.
3) Karthik: if you’re good with the pilot construct, I’ll draft the commercial attachment and routing to Legal/Finance.

If everyone agrees I’ll prepare the PDF quote + simple pilot SOW and we’ll aim to have it to them by EOD Friday.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Proposals | Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: redwood_pricing_options_v3.pdf
